prompt: A kite is flying on $80$ ft of taut string that makes a $40^\circ$ angle with the level ground. Which calculation gives the kite's height above the ground?
hint: The string is the hypotenuse; the height is the side opposite the $40^\circ$ angle.

hints.text: The string is the hypotenuse; the height is the side opposite the $40^\circ$ angle.

explanation: The taut string is the longest side of the triangle, so it is the hypotenuse: $80$ ft.
Height is opposite the $40^\circ$ angle, and opposite-over-hypotenuse is sine: $\sin 40^\circ = \frac{h}{80}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Eliminate the impossible
steps: The height can never exceed the $80$ ft of string, so choice D is out before any arithmetic.
Choice B is the horizontal distance and C uses the wrong pair of sides entirely — only A pairs the height with the hypotenuse.
